label: After the death: Holmes and Watson break the sad news to the terrified Miss Stoner
quote: how we broke the sad news to the terrified girl

labels.label: After that: Holmes means to remove Miss Stoner to some place of shelter
By the morning train: Holmes and Watson take Miss Stoner away towards Harrow

label: After the morning train: Miss Stoner is in the care of her aunt at Harrow
quote: to the care of her good aunt at Harrow

label: After the slow official inquiry: it concludes that the doctor met his fate while indiscreetly playing with a dangerous pet
quote: the slow process of official inquiry
note: Not ordered against the journey to Harrow or the journey back.

label: Next day: Holmes and Watson travel back
quote: as we travelled back next day
note: The text places the telling on this journey; it presumably follows taking Miss Stoner to Harrow.

label: Next day, travelling back: Holmes tells Watson of his wrong conclusion and how he came to think of a snake
quote: an entirely erroneous conclusion

label: Next day, travelling back: Holmes tells of the chair, the safe, the milk and the whipcord, and of the clang
quote: I had come to these conclusions before ever I had entered his room

label: Next day, travelling back: Watson says that Holmes drove the creature through the ventilator
quote: With the result of driving it through the ventilator

label: Next day, travelling back: Holmes says he is indirectly responsible for Dr. Roylott's death, and that it will not weigh heavily on him
quote: I am no doubt indirectly responsible

label: The fatal night: by the light of her match, Julia catches a hurried glimpse of something she calls a band, as Holmes reads it
quote: she had caught a hurried glimpse of by the light of her match

label: After his Eastern training, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott has the idea of a poison no chemical test could discover
quote: The idea of using a form of poison
note: Holmes's reconstruction; the text gives no date.

label: Before the whistles, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott trains the snake, probably with milk, to return when summoned
quote: He had trained it, probably by the use of the milk

label: At the hour he thinks best, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott puts the snake through the ventilator
quote: He would put it through this ventilator at the hour that he thought best
note: Holmes's reconstruction of something repeated over many nights.

label: As Holmes reads it: the snake crawls down the rope
quote: it would crawl down the rope

label: As Holmes reads it: the snake lands on the bed
quote: land on the bed

label: Before the morning light, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott must recall the snake by the whistle
quote: he must recall the snake before the morning light

label: Sooner or later, as Holmes reads it: the occupant of the bed falls victim to the snake
quote: sooner or later she must fall a victim
note: Holmes's reconstruction; not ordered in the text against the scream or the striking of the match.

labels.label: The fatal night, a few moments later: Helen seems to hear a clanging sound
The fatal night, a few moments later: the clang Helen hears, which Holmes reads as Dr. Roylott hastily closing his safe upon the snake

label: At Stoke Moran: Holmes reconsiders his position, once it is clear the danger could not come by window or door
quote: I instantly reconsidered my position

label: At Stoke Moran: Holmes's attention is drawn to the ventilator and the bell-rope
quote: My attention was speedily drawn

label: At Stoke Moran: Holmes suspects that the rope is a bridge for something coming through the hole to the bed
quote: the suspicion that the rope was there as a bridge

label: At Stoke Moran: the idea of a snake occurs to Holmes
quote: The idea of a snake instantly occurred to me

label: At Stoke Moran: Holmes thinks of the whistle
quote: Then I thought of the whistle

label: Before Holmes inspects it: Dr. Roylott has been in the habit of standing on his chair to reach the ventilator
quote: he had been in the habit of standing on it
note: Holmes's reading of the marks on the chair; repeated.

label: In Dr. Roylott's chamber: the safe, the saucer of milk and the loop of whipcord dispel Holmes's last doubts
quote: were enough to finally dispel any doubts

labels.label: Half an hour later: a very gentle, soothing sound, like a small jet of steam from a kettle
Half an hour later: the creature hisses, a very gentle sound like a small jet of steam from a kettle
That instant: Holmes lashes furiously with his cane at the bell-pull
That instant: Holmes attacks the creature with his cane at the bell-pull

label: That night: Holmes's blows drive the creature back through the ventilator, its temper roused
quote: driving it through the ventilator

note: ¶250–251: the snake, driven through the ventilator, turns upon its master at the other side. The text does not tie the bite to the cry of ¶238 in so many words.
